text: 🇲🇽🛢️ Pemex was the neoliberals' "petty cash." "They said they had responsible finances because their deficit was tiny. But who did they pile the debt onto? Pemex — with no results, just to prop up public spending. That's the truth." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Under Peña Nieto, Pemex debt climbed from $64 billion to $113 billion. This government cut it by $20 billion and says Pemex needs almost no federal support in 2027.

🇲🇽✊ "Where did they cut? In health, in education." "In the neoliberal era, health and education were exactly where they cut. The so-called 'austerity' never touched top officials' salaries or the money handed to the media." — President Claudia Sheinbaum She set that record against the 2027 budget: education +10.7%, science +13%, health +11.3%. The gap between the richest and poorest tenth fell from 34x in 2008 to 16x in 2024.

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum draws the red line in the USMCA talks. "Let the people of Mexico know: we will not sign anything that harms our sovereignty or our economy. What we're seeking are better trade terms." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the U.S. trade negotiations Mexico is pressing Washington to cut steel, aluminum and auto tariffs and add no new ones, while refusing to trade away sovereignty on the 54 "non-tariff barriers" on the table.

🚨🇲🇽 Media silence on the arrest of Cerimedo, the operator who targeted Sheinbaum. "Not a single outlet covered the arrest of Cerimedo, a partner in La Derecha Diario — who, by their own admission, set out to attack the President of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum At least five Latin American presidents have moved to distance themselves from the network. Sheinbaum says foreign electoral manipulation — and AI-driven disinformation — must be regulated.

🇲🇽⚖️ "The VAT is a very regressive tax" — Sheinbaum rejects raising it. "The VAT hits those who have the least the hardest. We do not agree with raising the VAT rate." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Since 2019 revenue has risen 2.7 trillion pesos with no tax hike — only by fighting evasion — versus 1.5 trillion under Peña Nieto's fiscal reform and gas hikes.
